articles.Title: Paras Public School, Bhawarna, organises exhibition titled ‘Vishay Sangam’
articles.Description: Paras Public School, Bhawarna, organised a grand educational exhibition titled ‘Vishay Sangam’. The exhibition aimed to provide a platform for students to showcase their talent, creativity, scientific temperament and multifaceted skills. The entire school campus was filled with an atmosphere of knowledge, imagination and innovation. The exhibition featured attractive and informative models, charts, projects and activities based on various subjects, including Science, English, Hindi, Sanskrit, Mathematics, Social Science, Computer Science, and Art and Craft. Dr Suresh Gautam, a retired scientist from CSK Himachal Pradesh Agricultural University, Palampur, was the chief guest. The programme commenced with the ceremonial lighting of the lamp before Goddess Saraswati by the chief guest, school Director Mahesh Chandra Katoch, Principal Neelam Rana and Dishaant Katoch. The chief guest visited the exhibition and observed the projects prepared by students across different subjects. He appreciated their skills, efforts, confidence and in-depth understanding of various concepts. Under the Science section, students presented a variety of models based on scientific concepts, including Newton’s Laws of Motion, Human Eye, Haemodialysis Model, Smart City, Transformer, London Hydraulic Bridge, Developed India, Life Cycle of a Butterfly and Chandrayaan-3. In Mathematics, various models illustrating different types of angles, ATMs and other mathematical concepts made the subject interesting and easy to understand. The English and Hindi sections attracted visitors through creative presentations related to language, literature, grammar and the lives of renowned personalities such as Munshi Premchand and Lata Mangeshkar. The Social Science section showcased attractive models and projects on topics such as volcanoes, Solar System, world globe, Indian economy and igloos. The Art and Craft section displayed the artistic abilities of students through beautiful handmade creations, including bamboo chairs, stools, bangle stands and several other craft items, which became special attractions of the exhibition. The Principal addressed the students and said the purpose of education was not merely to acquire bookish knowledge but also to develop the ability to think, understand, ask questions, generate new ideas and transform them into reality.
